name: Count
description: Counts rows, or counts the non-null values of an expression. Count() with no argument counts rows.

example.oquery: Customers: City, Count() CustomerCount, Count(LastName) NamedCustomerCount
example.explanation: Per city, counts all customers and only the customers that have a LastName value.

name: Sum
description: Returns the total of a numeric expression.

example.explanation: Per product, adds up the line amounts of all order items.

name: Avg
description: Returns the average of a numeric expression.

example.explanation: Per product, returns the average unit price across its order items.

name: Max
description: Returns the maximum value of a numeric expression.

example.explanation: Per product, returns the highest unit price it was ordered at.

name: Min
description: Returns the minimum value of a numeric expression.

example.explanation: Per product, returns the lowest unit price it was ordered at.

name: CountIf
description: Counts related rows that match a predicate. With two arguments, counts the non-null expression values on matching rows. The predicate is the last argument.

example.explanation: Per channel, counts only the orders whose Status is Open.

name: SumIf
description: Sums an expression over the rows that match a predicate.

example.explanation: Per product, adds up the quantity of order lines that have a discount.

name: AvgIf
description: Averages an expression over the rows that match a predicate.

example.explanation: Per product, averages the unit price only over order lines of 5 or more units.

name: MinIf
description: Returns the minimum of an expression over the rows that match a predicate.

example.explanation: Per product, returns the lowest unit price among order lines of 5 or more units.

name: MaxIf
description: Returns the maximum of an expression over the rows that match a predicate.

example.explanation: Per product, returns the highest unit price among discounted order lines.

name: MedicalLossRatio
description: Returns paid claims as a percentage of premium revenue, rounded to 2 decimal places. Returns null-safe 0 when claims are missing and avoids division by zero.

example.explanation: Per category, shows cost price as a percentage of unit price.

name: CountOver
description: Counts values within a window partition. Each detail row is kept, so the count is repeated on every row of the partition.

example.oquery: Sellers: Id, DepartmentId, CountOver(Id, DepartmentId) DepartmentHeadcount
example.explanation: Every employee row shows the headcount of their department, and no rows are collapsed.

name: SumOver
description: Sums values within a window partition while keeping each detail row.

example.oquery: Sellers: Id, DepartmentId, Salary, SumOver(Salary, DepartmentId) DepartmentPayroll
example.explanation: Every employee row shows the total payroll of their department.

name: AverageOver
description: Averages values within a window partition while keeping each detail row.

example.oquery: Sellers: Id, DepartmentId, Salary, AverageOver(Salary, DepartmentId) DepartmentAverageSalary
example.explanation: Every employee row shows the average salary of their department.

name: MaxOver
description: Returns the maximum within a window partition while keeping each detail row.

example.oquery: Sellers: Id, DepartmentId, Salary, MaxOver(Salary, DepartmentId) DepartmentMaximumSalary
example.explanation: Every employee row shows the highest salary in their department.

name: MinOver
description: Returns the minimum within a window partition while keeping each detail row.

example.oquery: Sellers: Id, DepartmentId, Salary, MinOver(Salary, DepartmentId) DepartmentMinimumSalary
example.explanation: Every employee row shows the lowest salary in their department.

name: Lag
signature: Lag(expression: Number, offset: Number, orderBy: String)
description: Returns the value of an expression from the row that is offset rows before the current row, in ascending orderBy order.

example.oquery: OrderItems: Id, UnitPrice, Lag(UnitPrice, <1>, Id) PreviousUnitPrice
example.explanation: Each order line shows the UnitPrice of the previous order line by Id.

name: WindowSum
sqlServerTemplate: SUM({1}) OVER (ORDER BY {2} ASC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
description: Returns a running total in ascending orderBy order.

example.oquery: OrderItems: Id, Quantity, WindowSum(Quantity, Id) RunningQuantity
example.explanation: Each order line shows the sum of quantities up to and including its Id.

name: Rank
sqlServerTemplate: RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY {1} ORDER BY {2} DESC)
description: Ranks rows within each partition by orderBy, highest value first. Tied values share a rank.

example.oquery: Products: Id, Category, UnitPrice, Rank(Category, UnitPrice) PriceRankInCategory
example.explanation: Within each category, the most expensive product gets rank 1.

name: RowNumber
sqlServerTemplate: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY {1} ORDER BY {2} DESC)
description: Numbers rows within each partition by orderBy, newest first. Each row gets a distinct number, even when values tie.

example.oquery: Orders: Id, UserId, OrderDate, RowNumber(UserId, OrderDate) OrderSequenceNewestFirst
example.explanation: For each customer, the latest order gets number 1.

name: NullIf
description: Returns null when the two values are equal; otherwise returns the first value. Use it to avoid division by zero.

example.explanation: A UnitPrice of 0 becomes null, so the division returns null instead of failing.

name: IfNull
description: Returns the first value when it is not null, otherwise returns the fallback.

example.explanation: Sellers without a salary show 0.

name: Concat
signature: Concat(first: String, separator: String, last: String)
description: Joins three text values in order, placing the separator between the first and last values.

example.explanation: Produces text such as 'Smith,John' for each employee.

name: MonthKey
description: Formats a date as a year-month key in YYYY-MM form, useful for grouping by month.

example.explanation: Groups revenue by month, with keys such as 2025-10.

name: Day
description: Returns the day-of-month part of a date.

example.explanation: Returns the day of the month when each employee was hired.

name: Month
description: Returns the month part of a date.

example.explanation: Returns the month number (1-12) when each employee was hired.

name: Year
description: Returns the year part of a date.

example.explanation: Returns the calendar year when each employee was hired.

name: DateAdd
description: Adds the given number of days to a date or date-time.

example.explanation: Each order's due date is 30 days after its OrderDate.

name: MonthAdd
description: Adds the given number of months to a date or date-time.

example.explanation: Each order renews 12 months after its OrderDate.

name: YearAdd
description: Adds the given number of years to a date or date-time.

example.explanation: Each order expires two years after its OrderDate.

name: YearsTo
sqlServerTemplate: (DATEDIFF(year, {1}, {2}) - CASE WHEN DATEPART(month, {2}) * 100 + DATEPART(day, {2}) < DATEPART(month, {1}) * 100 + DATEPART(day, {1}) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
description: Returns the number of completed years between startDate and endDate. A year is counted only after its anniversary date has passed.

example.explanation: An employee hired on 1 November 2020 has 4 completed years on 31 October 2025.

name: MonthsTo
sqlServerTemplate: (DATEDIFF(month, {1}, {2}) - CASE WHEN Day({2}) < Day({1}) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
description: Returns the number of completed calendar months between startDate and endDate.

example.explanation: Counts full months of service up to 31 October 2025.

name: DaysTo
description: Returns the number of completed days between startDate and endDate.

example.explanation: Counts whole days of service up to 31 October 2025.

name: YearsToNow
description: Returns the number of completed years from startDate until the current time. The result changes as time passes.

example.explanation: Shows each employee's completed years of service as of today.

name: MonthsToNow
description: Returns the number of completed months from startDate until the current time.

example.explanation: Shows each employee's completed months of service as of today.

name: DaysToNow
description: Returns the number of completed days from startDate until the current time.

example.explanation: Shows how many whole days have passed since each order's OrderDate.

name: Any
description: Returns true when a related collection has at least one row matching the optional predicate. Without a predicate, returns true when any related row exists.

example.explanation: Shows whether each customer has at least one open order.

name: NotAny
description: Returns true when no related collection row matches the optional predicate. It is the negative form of Any.

example.explanation: Shows the customers that have never placed an order.
